newsitem.title: USA: Boeing to review NTSB safety recommendations.
newsitem.headline: Boeing to review NTSB safety recommendations.

text.p: Boeing Co said it is reviewing the recommendations announced by the National Transportation Safety Board on Friday regarding proposed changes to the company's 747-type aircraft.
A spokesman for the Seattle-based aircraft maker said it will comply with the recommendations if the Federal Aviaition Administration decides to enforce them.

"Our position is any time safety is concerned, we prefer to go on the side of caution and we wil take whatever actions are necessary to support any of the directives that come down from the FAA," the spokesman said.

Earlier the FAA said it would issue an order next week to inspect wing fuel pump wiring on some early Boeing 747 aircraft. The agency said the potential wiring problem was uncovered during the investigation of the crash of Trans World Airways Flight 800 in the Atlantic off New York on July 17. However the FAA said it had no evidence to link the wiring to the crash.

In a written statement to the Federal Aviation Administration, the NTSB also recommended modifications to aircraft design to prevent fuel tank explosions. The FAA said it would urgently review the board's request.

The NTSB recommended the FAA consider aircraft design modifications, such as fire-extinguishing systems. It also recommended the addition of insulation between heat-generating equipment, such as air-conditioning ducts, and the fuel tanks.

The board also urged the FAA to consider a rule requiring an appropriate amount of fuel be kept in the center wing tank of the B-747. Whenever possible the fuel should be cool. There should be proper monitoring and maintenance of the tank's temperature, it said.
Boeing said some of the recommendations could extend beyond the 747 model to other aircraft, including those made by other manufacturers.
